tagline: A farm-colony road became a continental connection through a glacier-carved valley
intro: The Glenn Highway National Scenic Byway follows a glacier-carved corridor from Anchorage to Eureka Summit. For more than half its 135 miles, the road follows the braided Matanuska River, with the Chugach Mountains alongside the entire route. Alaska’s transportation department highlights that passage through glacial terrain, the colony farms of Palmer and the four mountain ranges visible at the summit. An archived federal byway guide allows 2.5 hours for the drive, or eight hours with visits along the way.

The road began in the 1930s as the Palmer Road, built to reach an agricultural colony. In May 1935, 203 families arrived from Michigan, Minnesota and Wisconsin, drawing lots for 40-acre farms. World War II changed the road’s reach: a military building program completed it to Glennallen and connected Anchorage to the continental highway system. Paving followed in the 1950s.

Leaving Anchorage, pass Eagle River and Chugiak before reaching Palmer’s colony farms. Beyond Palmer the road enters the Matanuska River Canyon, passing the former coal community of Sutton. Continue through Glacier View, where the Matanuska Glacier lies near the highway, to Eureka Summit. Here the byway ends at the highway’s 3,332-foot high point, on the divide between the Chugach and Talkeetna ranges.

moments.title: Palmer
moments.text: Forty-acre parcels were assigned by lot when 203 families came to Palmer in May 1935. Federal Emergency Relief Administration money moved them from Michigan, Minnesota and Wisconsin and helped turn a railroad siding into a planned town. They arrived by train and ship and spent their first Alaskan summer in tents. Many farms failed, but descendants of the colony families still live here and farms continue to operate. The annual Alaska State Fair carries agriculture into public view with contests for the largest vegetables, including cabbage, radishes, spinach and lettuce.

moments.title: Matanuska Glacier
moments.text: Matanuska Glacier feeds the river the byway follows. This valley glacier measures 27 miles long and four miles wide and lies near the Glenn Highway at Glacier View. Its ice flows about a foot each day. Over the three decades ending in 2007, its terminus changed little because ice was being lost from the lower glacier.

moments.title: Eureka Summit
moments.text: Eureka Summit is the Glenn Highway’s high point at 3,332 feet, on the divide between the Chugach and Talkeetna mountain ranges. It also marks the end of the national scenic byway. Alaska’s transportation department identifies four ranges in the view here: the Alaska Range, Chugach Mountains, Talkeetna Mountains and Wrangell-St. Elias Mountains.
moments.notice: Four ranges meet the view at Eureka Summit: Alaska, Chugach, Talkeetna and Wrangell-St. Elias.
